missionPremise: Operator Nick ruled 2026-08-31 'retire pe-billing.ts'. The install-scoped seam POST /api/brokerage/v1/property-explorer/billing/checkout resolves stripePriceIdForTier to STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID, the retired pre-ladder Pro price, so any request reaching it opens a Stripe checkout at an amount that is not on the locked ladder. Stripe being in test mode is the only thing between it and real money. hauska-map PR #325 retired the client half under P-97 and explicitly named the two BFF paths it left, which is the same-card retirement rule working as intended. Sources: the compiled dispatch; the doc_repo scope correction committed at 41278c7; apps/property-explorer/src/lib/billingClient.ts:144-153 read at source.

LESSON: A shell one-liner is not an instrument. grep -c '[^\x00-\x7F]' in bash does NOT interpret hex escapes; it matches the literal characters x, 0, 7 and F, and reported nearly every line of every file as non-ASCII. The wrong answer looked plausible. Replaced with a node scan carrying a known-positive control (api/spine.ts, which really does hold 33 non-ASCII code points).

A retirement guard should re-implement the CONSUMER'S matching rule, not grep for the retired string. spine.ts admits a path when an allowlist entry equals it or prefixes it, so re-adding 'api/brokerage/v1/property-explorer' restores the permission without ever containing the word "billing". A literal grep passes on that; the predicate does not.

Extract an array literal by depth-counting the brackets with strings and comments skipped, never by indexOf("]"). Proven necessary: against the naive extractor, a nested array truncated the scan to three entries and a "]" inside a string produced an empty extraction - in both cases the guard would have reported clean on a tree carrying the violation.

The pair "an allowed sibling still reaches upstream" plus "the retired path is declined" is what turns a 403 from an assumption into a measurement. The map-data POST returning an upstream zod error is what makes the billing POST 403 mean something.

A probe can prove a Vercel function is deployed without touching anything downstream: send the request the function itself rejects. The header-less pe-billing POST returned the function's own install_id_required, which no absent route could produce, with zero upstream contact - and the 404 on a made-up route proves present and absent are distinguishable on that host.
DEAD-END: Byte-exact string replacement against a Windows checkout of this repo. The working tree is CRLF via autocrlf while the blobs are LF, so LF-terminated match strings fail. It failed CLOSED, which was correct, but the working method is a line-oriented splice that re-uses each line's existing terminator.
Using git checkout -- to restore files after a violation test. That would discard the lane's working-tree changes, which ARE the deliverable. Back up the bytes and rewrite them instead.
